mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying, the Exalted: (ما ودعك): (ما) [with its clause] is the answer to the oath.
His saying (ألم يجدك يتيما): the kāf and (يتيما) are two objects of (يجد); likewise (ووجدك ضالا) and (ووجدك عائلا).
His saying (وما قلى): the object is omitted, i.e. "and He has not detested you", i.e. "and He has not hated you". (ودع) is used only with doubling; one does not say (ودع) [wadaʿa]. Sībawayh said: they dispensed with it by (ترك).

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying (فأما اليتيم فلا تقهر): (اليتيم) is accusative governed by (تقهر), and it properly belongs after the fāʾ; its implied form is "Whatever may be, do not oppress the orphan." Its like is (وأما السائل فلا تنهر). Had there been a hāʾ with (تقهر) and (تنهر), the preferred choice in (اليتيم) and (السائل) would be the nominative, with the accusative permissible; with the hāʾ omitted, only the accusative is permissible. (اليتيم) and (السائل) are nouns indicating the genus.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying (وأما بنعمة ربك فحدث): the bāʾ is attached to (حدث), and its implied place is after it; the implied form is "Whatever may be, speak of the favour of your Lord."
His saying (ولسوف يعطيك ربك): the second object is omitted, as you say "I gave you" and stop; so the implied form is "He will give you what you want, and you will be satisfied."
